titulo: Prepositions of place / Prepositions of time: on/in/at
titulo_es: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)
descripcion_es: When to use in, on and at to talk about time and place.
resumen: In, on and at nearly always translate Spanish “en”, but they are shared out according to how precise the time or place is: at for exact points, on for days and surfaces, in for long periods and enclosed or large spaces.

filas: at 8 o'clock, at night, at the weekend, at Christmas
on Monday, on 5 May, on my birthday, on Friday evening
months, seasons, years, parts of the day
in July, in winter, in 2024, in the morning
a specific point or place, addresses
at the bus stop, at home, at work, at 12 Baker Street
on the table, on the wall, on the second floor, on Oxford Street
in the kitchen, in a box, in Madrid, in Spain

items: No preposition: this/next/last/every + time (next week, last Monday, every day).
in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night.
Means of transport: in a car / in a taxi, but on a bus / on a train / on a plane.

ejemplos.frase: The meeting is at ten on Thursday.
ejemplos.traduccion: La reunión es a las diez el jueves.

ejemplos.frase: Your glasses are on the kitchen table.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tus gafas están en la mesa de la cocina.

ejemplos.frase: I'll wait for you at the station.
She lives in a small village in Galicia.
ejemplos.traduccion: Vive en un pueblo pequeño de Galicia.

ejemplos.frase: We don't work at the weekend.
ejemplos.traduccion: No trabajamos el fin de semana.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With days of the week you use on.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I'll call you the next week.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With next, last, this and every there is no preposition and no article.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.frase: The film starts ___ half past nine.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: at is used with times and specific moments. The clue is half past nine, an exact clock time. That is why it is at half past nine. At is used with all clock times (at 8 o'clock, at noon, at midnight), since they are precise points in time.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película empieza a las nueve y media.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In is for long periods (months, years, parts of the day); with an exact time it is at.
On is for days and dates; with a clock time you use at.
A calque of Spanish “a las”: the time is introduced with at, not with to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: in is used with months, seasons, years and parts of the day. The clue is February, a month, that is, a long period within which the action happens. That is why it is in February. Remember that in English months are always written with a capital letter.
ejercicios.traduccion: Siempre vamos a esquiar en febrero.

errores_previstos.explicacion: On is used with days and specific dates (on 5 February); with the month alone, in.
At is for times and specific moments; with a month you use in.
No article is used with the name of the month: in February.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: on is used with days and dates. The clue is Sundays, a day of the week; in the plural it shows something that happens every Sunday. That is why it is on Sundays, which corresponds to Spanish “los domingos”. In Spanish no preposition is used, so Spanish speakers tend to leave it out or use in.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “en”: with days of the week you use on.
At is for clock times; with days you use on.
A calque of Spanish “los domingos”: English uses no article, but the preposition on.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table: on is used with surfaces. The clue is the wall: the picture hangs on the surface of the wall, in contact with it, not inside it. That is why it is on the wall, just like on the table or on the floor. In the wall would mean something built into the wall, such as a safe.
ejercicios.traduccion: Hay un cuadro en la pared.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In would mean that the picture is inside the wall; on a surface it is on.
At is for specific points or places; with surfaces you use on.
Over means “above, higher than without touching”; a hanging picture is on the wall.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table: in is used with large spaces, cities and countries. The clue is Mexico, a country, which is thought of as a territory within which people live. That is why it is in Mexico, just like in Spain or in Madrid.

errores_previstos.explicacion: At is for specific points (at the bus stop); with countries you use in.
On is for surfaces and streets; with countries you use in.
The preposition has been left in Spanish: in English it is in.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with in, on or at.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's note on the exception: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night. The clue is night, the only part of the day that takes at, and with no article. It is a fixed expression that you should learn by heart as it is. In the night exists, but it refers to a moment during a particular night (I woke up in the night).
ejercicios.traduccion: No puedo dormir por la noche.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The other parts of the day take in the, but night is the exception: at night.
The fixed expression is at night, with no article.
By night exists in literary style (“during the night”), but the normal expression is at night.

ejercicios.frase: Meet me ___ the entrance of the museum.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table: at is used with a specific point or place. The clue is the entrance, a precise meeting point, not an enclosed space that you go into. That is why it is at the entrance, just like at the bus stop or at the door.
ejercicios.traduccion: Quedamos en la entrada del museo.

por_opcion.in: Incorrect: in would mean being inside a space; the entrance is a meeting point, at.
por_opcion.on: Incorrect: on is for surfaces or streets; it does not fit a meeting point.
por_opcion.at: Correct: at for a specific meeting point.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table: in is used with enclosed spaces (in the kitchen, in a box). The clue is the fridge, a closed container that holds the milk. That is why it is in the fridge. On the fridge would mean “on top of the fridge”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La leche está en la nevera.

por_opcion.in: Correct: inside an enclosed space, in the fridge.
por_opcion.on: Incorrect: on the fridge would mean that the milk is on top of the fridge, on its surface.
por_opcion.at: Incorrect: at is used for points or places, not for the inside of a container.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's note that no preposition is used with this, next, last and every + a time expression. The clue is next: next month already works on its own as a time adverbial, with no preposition or article. That is why it is We're going to Rome next month. “The next month” is used in narratives to mean “the following month” after another moment, not “the coming month” counting from today.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With next no preposition or article is used.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vamos a Roma el mes que viene.

por_opcion.next month: Correct: with next there is no preposition or article.
por_opcion.in next month: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “en el próximo mes”; with next no preposition is used.
por_opcion.the next month: Incorrect with this meaning: the next month means “the following month” in relation to another moment in the story; for “the coming month” from today you say next month.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's note on the parts of the day: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night. The clue is the evening, a part of the day with an article, which requires in. Bear in mind that evening is the last part of the day and the beginning of the night, from about six o'clock, whereas afternoon is the time after lunch (both are Spanish “tarde”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Parts of the day: in the evening.
ejercicios.traduccion: Suelo leer por la tarde (a última hora).

por_opcion.at: Incorrect: at is only used with night (at night); with the evening it is in.
por_opcion.on: Incorrect in general: on is used with a specific day (on Friday evening), but with the evening alone it is only in.
por_opcion.in: Correct: parts of the day with an article, in the evening.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: in is used with years. The clue is 2005, a year, a long period. On is only used with days or full dates: My sister was born on 3 May 2005. That is why, with the year alone, the preposition is in.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: on is for days and full dates; with the year alone, in.
At is for times and specific moments; with years you use in.
The preposition is right, but Spanish “nacer” in English is be born: was born.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: on is used with days of the week. The clue is Friday, a specific day. That is why it is on Friday. The mistake with in is a calque of Spanish “en”, which English keeps for long periods.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with days of the week you use on.
At is for times and moments; with days, on.
A calque of Spanish “el viernes”: English uses the preposition on, with no article.

respuestas: He is not at home now.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table, which gives at home as an example: with home, work and school, seen as places of activity, you use at and no article. The clue is home, which forms a fixed expression with at. In home is incorrect, although in the house does exist. All three negative forms are accepted: He's not, He isn't and He is not.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the fixed expression is at home.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He's not at the home now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The expression at home has no article.
On is for surfaces; the fixed expression is at home.

respuestas: I start work at seven on Mondays
On Mondays I start work at seven
I start work on Mondays at seven
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the time table: at with clock times (at seven) and on with days (on Mondays). The clue is that there are two time adverbials and each one takes its own preposition. The basic order is subject + verb + object (I start work) and then the adverbials; on Mondays can go at the end, before at seven or at the beginning of the sentence.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: At for the time and on for the day.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los lunes empiezo a trabajar a las siete.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I start work on seven at Mondays
errores_previstos.explicacion: The prepositions have been swapped: at goes with the time (at seven) and on with the day (on Mondays).

errores_previstos.respuesta: On Mondays at seven start I work
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject goes before the verb: I start work.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I start at seven work on Mondays
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object work goes right after the verb start, before the time adverbials.

respuestas: The children are in the garden
Are the children in the garden
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the place table: in is used with bounded or enclosed spaces. The clue is the garden, a space with limits within which the children are. That is why it is in the garden. The order is subject + verb + place adverbial: The children are in the garden. With are at the front you get the question, which is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños están en el jardín.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children are the garden in
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition goes before its complement: in the garden.

errores_previstos.respuesta: In the garden the children are
errores_previstos.explicacion: An unnatural order in English: the verb cannot go at the end; the normal order is The children are in the garden.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The children in the garden are
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb are goes after the subject and before the place adverbial.

descripcion_larga_es: In, on and at nearly always translate Spanish “en”, but English shares them out according to how precise the time or place is: at for clock times and specific points, on for days and surfaces, in for months, years and enclosed spaces. They are used in almost every sentence. They are hard for Spanish speakers because Spanish has a single preposition and because there are fixed expressions (at night, at home) that must be learnt by heart.

contexto.que_es: They are the three basic prepositions for placing something in time or space. They work as a scale of precision: at for an exact point (a time, an address), on for a day or a surface, and in for a long period or a space that contains something. There are also fixed expressions and cases with no preposition (next week, last Monday).
contexto.por_que_importa: They appear constantly when giving appointments, timetables, dates or addresses. A mistake (“in Friday”, “on 2005”, “in home”) rarely prevents understanding, but it is very noticeable and sounds basic. Choosing well can change the nuance: at the cinema (there to see a film, as a place of activity) versus in the cinema (inside the building).
contexto.cuando_se_usa: Whenever you say when or where something happens. The signals are the type of word that follows: a clock time requires at, a day of the week or a date requires on, a month, a year or a city requires in. Spanish speakers tend to use in for everything, like Spanish “en”, and to add a preposition before next or last (“in next month”).
